title: Monetary reform in the Soviet Union.
text: A monetary reform of the Soviet ruble, also known as the Khrushchev reform, took place on 1 January 1961. The reform consisted of the devaluation of the ruble against the United States dollar, and the redenomination of the ruble at a ratio of 10 to 1.
wiki: Monetary reform in the Soviet Union, 1961

title: United States President Dwight D. Eisenhower announces that the United States has severed diplomatic and consular relations with Cuba (Cuba–United States relations are restored in 2015).
text: Dwight David Eisenhower was the 34th president of the United States, serving from 1953 to 1961, and a U.S. Army general who commanded the Allied Expeditionary Force in the invasions of Normandy and Nazi Germany in World War II. Eisenhower graduated from West Point in 1915. During World War I, he was denied a request to serve in Europe and instead commanded a unit that trained tank crews.

title: Aero Flight 311 (Koivulahti air disaster): Douglas DC-3C OH-LCC of Finnish airline Aero crashes near Kvevlax (Koivulahti), on approach to Vaasa Airport in Finland, killing all 25 on board, due to pilot error: an investigation finds that…
text: Aero Flight 311, often referred to as the Kvevlax air disaster, was a scheduled domestic passenger flight operated by Aero O/Y between Kronoby and Vaasa in Finland. The aircraft, a Douglas DC-3, crashed in the municipality Kvevlax (Finnish: Koivulahti), nowadays part of Korsholm (Finnish: Mustasaari) on 3 January 1961, killing all twenty-five people on board.

title: After the 1960 military coup, General Cemal Gürsel forms the new government of Turkey (25th government).
text: Cemal Gürsel was a Turkish military officer and politician who was the president of Turkey from 1960 to 1966 after taking power in a coup d'état.

title: Following a four-day conference in Casablanca, five African chiefs of state announce plans for a NATO-type African organization to ensure common defense. The Charter of Casablanca involves the Casablanca Group: Morocco, the United Arab…
text: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is an intergovernmental military alliance between 32 member states (thirty in Europe and two in North America). Founded in the aftermath of World War II, NATO was established with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty in 1949.

title: In France, a referendum supports Charles de Gaulle's policies on independence for Algeria.
text: A referendum on self-determination for Algeria was held in France on 8 January 1961. Self-determination was approved by 75% of voters overall and 70% in Algeria.

title: British authorities announce they have uncovered a large Soviet spy ring, the Portland spy ring, in London.
text: The Portland spy ring was an espionage group active in the UK between 1953 and 1961. It comprised five people who obtained classified research documents from the Admiralty Underwater Weapons Establishment on the Isle of Portland, Dorset, and passed them to the Soviet Union.

title: Patrice Lumumba of the Republic of Congo is assassinated.
text: Patrice Émery Lumumba was a Congolese politician, independence leader, and revolutionary who served as the first prime minister of the First Congolese Republic (modern day Democratic Republic of the Congo) from June until September 1960, following his party's success in the May 1960 election. Lumumba was the leader of the Congolese National Movement (MNC) from 1958 until his assassination in 1961.

title: John F. Kennedy is inaugurated as the 35th President of the United States, becoming the second-youngest president to be sworn in.
text: John Fitzgerald Kennedy, also known as JFK, was the 35th president of the United States, serving from 1961 until his assassination in 1963. A member of the Democratic Party, he represented Massachusetts in both houses of the U.S. Congress before his presidency.

title: Congress of Venezuela adopts a new constitution (in force until 1999).
text: The Constitution of Venezuela of 1961 was approved on January 16, 1961, by the then Congress of the Republic with the affirmative vote of the four main political forces of the country at that time, Democratic Action, Democratic Republican Union, COPEI and the Communist Party of Venezuela. It came into force on January 23 of the same year in commemoration of the return to democracy in Venezuela on January 23, 1958.

title: Acting to halt 'leftist excesses', a junta composed of two army officers and four civilians takes over El Salvador, ousting another junta that had ruled for three months.
text: A military dictatorship is a type of dictatorship where supreme power is held and exercised by a member of the armed forces. Military dictatorships are usually led by the commander-in-chief of the military or the leading figure of a military junta.

title: Soviet submarine S-80 sinks in the Barents Sea, killing all 68 crew.
text: S-80 was a diesel-electric submarine of the Soviet Navy. Its keel was laid down on 13 March 1950 at Krasnoye Sormovo as a Project 613 unit.

title: Supercar, the first family sci-fi TV series filmed in Supermarionation, debuts on ATV in the UK.
text: Supermarionation is a style of television and film production employed by British company AP Films (later Century 21 Productions) in its puppet TV series and feature films of the 1960s. These productions were created by Gerry and Sylvia Anderson and filmed at APF's studios on the Slough Trading Estate.

title: Ham, a 37-pound (17-kg) male chimpanzee, is rocketed into space aboard Mercury-Redstone 2, in a test of the Project Mercury spacecraft, designed to carry United States astronauts into space.
text: Ham, a chimpanzee also known as Ham the Chimp and Ham the Astrochimp, was the first ape launched into space. On January 31, 1961, Ham flew a suborbital flight on the Mercury-Redstone 2 mission, part of the U.S. space program's Project Mercury.

title: The United States tests its first Minuteman I intercontinental ballistic missile.
text: The LGM-30 Minuteman is an American land-based intercontinental ballistic missile in service with the Air Force Global Strike Command. As of 2025, the LGM-30G (Version 3) is the only land-based ICBM in service in the United States and represents the land leg of the U.S. nuclear triad, along with the Trident II submarine-launched ballistic missile (SLBM) and nuclear weapons carried by long-range strategic bombers.

title: The Portuguese Colonial War begins in Angola.
text: The Portuguese Colonial War, also known in Portugal as the Overseas War (Guerra do Ultramar) or in the former colonies as the War of Liberation (Guerra de Libertação), and also known as the Angolan, Guinea-Bissau and Mozambican Wars of Independence, was a 13-year-long conflict fought between Portugal's military and the emerging nationalist movements in Portugal's African colonies between 1961 and 1974. The Portugu…

title: February 5–9 – In Congo, President Joseph Kasa-Vubu names Joseph Iléo as the new Prime Minister.
text: The First Congolese Republic refers to the political regime in the country known as the Republic of the Congo and, later, Democratic Republic of the Congo (French: République démocratique du Congo) between independence in 1960 and the 1965 coup d'état by General Joseph-Désiré Mobutu. Its existence also coincided with the Congo Crisis.

title: Italian sculptor Alfredo Fioravanti goes to the United States consulate in Rome to confess that he was part of the team that forged the Etruscan terracotta warriors in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
text: The United States has the second largest number of active diplomatic posts of any country in the world after the People's Republic of China, including 272 bilateral posts in 174 countries, as well as 11 permanent missions to international organizations and seven other posts (as of May 2025). It maintains "interests sections" (in other states' embassies) in Afghanistan, Iran and North Korea.
wiki: List of diplomatic missions of the United States

title: Release of British film The Rebel starring Tony Hancock, satirizing artistic pretensions.
text: The Rebel is a 1961 British satirical comedy film directed by Robert Day and starring Tony Hancock. It was written by Ray Galton and Alan Simpson.

title: Publication in the United States of Irving Stone's biographical novel of Michelangelo, The Agony and the Ecstasy.
text: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni, known mononymously as Michelangelo, was an Italian sculptor, painter, architect, and poet of the High Renaissance. He was born in the Republic of Florence but was mostly active in Rome from his 30s onwards.

title: May 29–June 17 – War Babies exhibition at the Huysman Gallery in Los Angeles featuring the work of Joe Goode, Larry Bell, Ed Bereal and Ron Miyashiro. Controversy generated by the exhibition's poster leads to the gallery closing down soon…
text: Larry Bell is an American contemporary artist and sculptor. He is best known for his glass boxes and large-scaled illusionistic sculptures.

title: Goya's Portrait of the Duke of Wellington is stolen from the National Gallery in London, three weeks after first going on display there, intended as ransom in Kempton Bunton's campaign for free television licences for pensioners. It is…
text: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes was a Spanish romantic painter and printmaker. He is considered the most important Spanish artist of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
